title: Google Sheets
description: Google Sheets as the signed-in Workspace user: read and write values in spreadsheets they can open, by id — Finance and attendance spreadsheets

guide.summary: Each caller's own spreadsheets by id: A1 ranges, cell-paged reads, RAW or USER_ENTERED writes, raw batchUpdate.
guide.content:
# Google Sheets usage

Acts as the signed-in person in their own Google Sheets through Workspace delegation: it reaches only spreadsheets they can open, starting from an id.

Connection purpose: Finance and attendance spreadsheets

## Whose spreadsheets

Every call acts as the Workspace account deployment config maps the caller
to; an agent acts as the owner of the pool it came through, unless the deployment fixes one shared account that every caller, agent or person, acts as. No argument
names an account. A call with none mapped fails `auth_required`; only an operator can change
that. An id that is
unknown or not shared with this person fails `connector_call_failed` (or
`provider_permission_denied` when Google refuses access) — Google does not
say which; check the id or ask the owner to share it.

## Finding a spreadsheet

- Sheets cannot list or search files. Find one by name with a Google Drive
  search, or take the id from its URL (between `/d/` and `/edit`).
- `get_spreadsheet` first: sheet titles, ids, grid sizes, and named ranges,
  so ranges are named right rather than guessed.

## Ranges

- A1 notation. Quote a sheet title with spaces or punctuation:
  `'Q3 Budget'!A1:D20`, doubling any `'` inside it. A bare title is the
  whole sheet; `Sheet1!B:B` a whole column; a named range works by name.
- `get_values` pages by whole rows under `maxCells` and `maxBytes`:
  page with `page.nextCursor` and the same spreadsheetId, ranges, and
  render options. A range with explicit rows (`A1:D500`, `B:D`) resumes
  where it stopped; a sheet title or named range is re-read and its earlier
  rows skipped, so `rowOffset` says how far into Google's echoed range the
  page starts.
- A row too wide or too large for one page is refused, not cut: narrow the
  columns or lower `maxCellChars`. The default `maxBytes` is what
  `execute_code` can receive; raise it only for a direct `call_tool`
  read.
- A cell over 5000 characters ends with a truncation marker;
  read it alone with `maxCellChars` for the rest. Reduce inside
  `execute_code` before returning a large read.

## Writing

- `valueInputOption` is required: `RAW` stores text as given;
  `USER_ENTERED` parses it as typed, so a leading `=` makes a formula. Use
  RAW for data from outside the spreadsheet.
- In written rows, `null` leaves a cell as it was and `""` empties it.
- `append_values` inserts rows below the table and overwrites nothing;
  `update_values` and `batch_update_values` overwrite the cells they
  cover; `clear_values` empties values but keeps formatting.
- `batch_update_spreadsheet` takes Google's own Request objects for
  everything else (formatting, sorting, deleting rows or sheets); it is
  atomic, always needs approval, and can destroy data. Replies too large
  to return come back cut to their kind, ids, and counts with a `note`;
  the requests still applied, so never send them again to see the rest.
- Sheets has no revision check on writes: edits are last-writer-wins, so a
  person editing the same cells meanwhile is overwritten without warning.
  Read just before writing over anything a person may be editing.
- Moving, sharing, or deleting a spreadsheet file is Drive's job.

tools.name: get_spreadsheet
tools.description: Get a spreadsheet's title, sheets (ids, titles, grid sizes), and named ranges as A1, never cell values. To find one by name, search Drive; Sheets cannot list.

spreadsheetId.description: Spreadsheet id: the part of its URL between /d/ and /edit. Find one by name with a Drive search; Sheets cannot list.

raw.description: Return Google's untouched spreadsheet metadata — formatting, protections, charts — instead of the projection. Never cell values.

tools.name: get_values
tools.description: Read cell values from one or more A1 ranges as rows, paged by cell count. Long cells are cut with a marker; no formatting, notes, or formulas unless asked.

spreadsheetId.description: Spreadsheet id: the part of its URL between /d/ and /edit. Find one by name with a Drive search; Sheets cannot list.

items.description: A1 notation: Sheet1!A1:D20, 'Q3 Budget'!B:B, a sheet title alone, or a named range.

ranges.description: Ranges to read, 1 to 20, returned in this order.

valueRenderOption.description: FORMATTED_VALUE (default) as displayed; UNFORMATTED_VALUE as raw numbers; FORMULA shows formulas instead of results.

dateTimeRenderOption.description: Dates when valueRenderOption is not FORMATTED_VALUE: SERIAL_NUMBER (Google's default, days since 1899-12-30) or FORMATTED_STRING.

maxCells.description: Cells per page, 1 to 10000; defaults to 2000. Connecta's cap: Sheets returns whole ranges, so this pages by whole rows.

maxBytes.description: Bytes of the whole page as JSON; defaults to 196608, what execute_code can receive. Raise it, to 4194304, only for a direct call_tool read.

maxCellChars.description: Characters kept per cell, to 50000 (Sheets' cell limit, so the whole cell); defaults to 5000. Longer cells end with a marker.

cursor.description: Opaque page.nextCursor from the previous page. Pass it back unchanged with the same spreadsheetId, ranges, and render options.

tools.name: update_values
tools.description: Write rows of values into one A1 range, overwriting what is there. Cells past the given rows are untouched; to add rows below a table use append_values.

spreadsheetId.description: Spreadsheet id: the part of its URL between /d/ and /edit. Find one by name with a Drive search; Sheets cannot list.

range.description: A1 notation: Sheet1!A1:D20, 'Q3 Budget'!B:B, a sheet title alone, or a named range; the top-left cell is where the first value goes.

items.description: One row's cells, left to right.

values.description: Rows of cells, top to bottom. null leaves a cell unchanged; "" empties it. At most 50000 cells per call, connecta's cap.

valueInputOption.description: RAW stores each value literally; USER_ENTERED parses it as if typed, so =SUM(A1:A3) is a formula and 2026-10-06 a date.

tools.name: batch_update_values
tools.description: Write values into several A1 ranges in one call, overwriting each. All succeed or none do. For formatting or structure use batch_update_spreadsheet.

spreadsheetId.description: Spreadsheet id: the part of its URL between /d/ and /edit. Find one by name with a Drive search; Sheets cannot list.

range.description: A1 notation: Sheet1!A1:D20, 'Q3 Budget'!B:B, a sheet title alone, or a named range.

items.description: One row's cells, left to right.

values.description: Rows of cells, top to bottom. null leaves a cell unchanged; "" empties it. At most 50000 cells per call, connecta's cap.

valueInputOption.description: RAW stores each value literally; USER_ENTERED parses it as if typed, so =SUM(A1:A3) is a formula and 2026-10-06 a date.

tools.name: append_values
tools.description: Append rows after the last row of the table in an A1 range, inserting new rows so nothing below is overwritten. Returns where they landed.

spreadsheetId.description: Spreadsheet id: the part of its URL between /d/ and /edit. Find one by name with a Drive search; Sheets cannot list.

range.description: A1 notation: Sheet1!A1:D20, 'Q3 Budget'!B:B, a sheet title alone, or a named range; Sheets finds the table in it and appends below its last row.

items.description: One row's cells, left to right.

values.description: Rows of cells, top to bottom. null leaves a cell unchanged; "" empties it. At most 50000 cells per call, connecta's cap.

valueInputOption.description: RAW stores each value literally; USER_ENTERED parses it as if typed, so =SUM(A1:A3) is a formula and 2026-10-06 a date.

tools.name: clear_values
tools.description: Clear the values in one or more A1 ranges, keeping formatting, notes, and validation. The values are gone; nothing is deleted or shifted.

spreadsheetId.description: Spreadsheet id: the part of its URL between /d/ and /edit. Find one by name with a Drive search; Sheets cannot list.

items.description: A1 notation: Sheet1!A1:D20, 'Q3 Budget'!B:B, a sheet title alone, or a named range.

tools.name: create_spreadsheet
tools.description: Create a new spreadsheet in the user's My Drive root, optionally with named sheets. It is not shared or moved; that is Drive's job.

sheetTitles.description: Sheet tabs to start with, in order; omit for Google's one sheet, Sheet1.

tools.name: add_sheet
tools.description: Add a new, empty sheet tab to a spreadsheet. Fails if the title is taken; it never renames, replaces, or copies an existing sheet.

spreadsheetId.description: Spreadsheet id: the part of its URL between /d/ and /edit. Find one by name with a Drive search; Sheets cannot list.

title.description: The new tab's title, unique in the spreadsheet.

index.description: Tab position, 0 first; omit to add it last.

rowCount.description: Rows in the grid; Google defaults to 1,000.

columnCount.description: Columns in the grid; Google defaults to 26.

tools.name: batch_update_spreadsheet
tools.description: Apply raw Sheets batchUpdate requests — formatting, merges, sorts, deleting sheets or rows, protections — atomically. The approval-gated hatch; it can destroy data.

spreadsheetId.description: Spreadsheet id: the part of its URL between /d/ and /edit. Find one by name with a Drive search; Sheets cannot list.

items.description: One Sheets Request with exactly one kind set, as Google documents it: { repeatCell: {…} }, { deleteDimension: {…} }, { sortRange: {…} }.

requests.description: Sheets API Request objects, 1 to 100, applied in order; all succeed or none do.
